title: “Fund the dog‑shit scientist” actually worked
summary:
The most insane part is it’s not a metaphor: @visakanv openly rallied Twitter to bankroll @ultimape’s “eat literal dog shit for science” gut microbiome experiment — and people just… did it. Visa framed him as a rare legit hobbyist researcher (“I’d give him a whole lab if I could”), then admitted he was “burying the lede” because the lede was coprophagia with a bibliography.

The arc is weirdly wholesome. It starts with @ultimape’s earlier “metabrain” network visualizations (2020) establishing his autodidact/mad-scientist persona, then snaps into fundraising in Aug 2021 when he says he needs microbiota testing and a $400 fridge to keep the month-long experiment sanitary. Within hours he reports $430 on PayPal (“having a fridge… will significantly de-risk the experiment”), and @Malcolm_Ocean brags he threw in $40 and set up ongoing Patreon. Visa’s follow-up is basically: don’t overthink thank-yous, just publish results. By Mar 2022, @ultimape posts Viome results claiming his “biological age” moved 37→27 based on IGF‑1/mTOR/sirtuins/AMPK, then pivots into ever-more-absurd-but-earnest tooling like a DIY sperm-tracking grant proposal (“jizz camera, give money”) and names it Project Viril.

What peaks later is the “artifact” phase: longform essays, proposals, and eventually (July 2025) @ultimape announcing Patreon approved his account at a sustainable tier — his own phrasing: “autistic citizen scientist bootstrapped a crowd-sourced basic income by eating dog shit.” The thread doesn’t really die from backlash; it just settles into a victory lap and gratitude loop, with @ultimape quoting the original Visa tweet like closing the circle. Why care: it’s a case study in how a niche internet community can straight-up create patronage rails for citizen science — and how a gross meme can be both the marketing hook and the funding engine.
